I have been working this land my whole life. My father farmed here before me, and I know this soil the way I know my own hands. I don't read books about farming — I read the sky, the soil, and what my neighbors are doing. At 70, just me and my wife at home, I cannot work as hard as I used to. I have to be careful about what I take on.

My 6.8 mu: I will put 2 mu in cotton and keep 4.8 mu for wheat and maize rotation. Cotton is hard work — picking, thinning, spraying — but it brings in cash money that grain alone cannot. Still, I am getting old. 2 mu is what I can manage without hiring help, which costs money I don't want to spend.

For wheat, I will use the same improved seed I have bought from the township seed shop for many years — not the newest variety, the one I know. I will plough before planting in October as always. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea at jointing stage. I will pump the well water 3 times: before freeze, at jointing, at heading. Two or three pesticide sprays, more if aphids are bad in spring. I expect around 430 jin per mu if the weather holds.

For summer maize after the wheat harvest in June, I use hybrid seed — everyone does now, the yield is better. I rotary till after wheat and plant quickly. Maize needs less water than wheat here, maybe twice from the well unless it is a dry summer. Fertilizer at planting and one topdressing. Two pesticide applications for corn borer and fall armyworm.

For cotton on my 2 mu, I will plough in spring and plant in late April after the cold passes. Cotton needs the most care — many waterings, many sprays. I will irrigate 4 times and spray 7 or 8 times through the season for bollworm, aphids, spider mites. I have done this for decades. I apply more fertilizer on cotton than anything else because it must keep producing new bolls.
